title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC0LE_1RD1RA_0RE1RF_1LF0RC_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC0LE_1RD1RA_0RE1RF_1LF0RC_0LA---.
intro: This six-state machine was one of the bbchallenge holdouts. It halts: busycoq pull request 106 proves it in Rocq (compiled here). This page describes what its run looks like at the level of words and counters and how the proof follows it. The description before the proof comes from simulation; this repository's own work proves nothing beyond the bounded runs.
verdict: Decided by an outside Rocq proof: it halts. Busycoq pull request 106 (Alex Havrilla of DeepMind, 2026-11-19) proves this in Rocq, and we compiled it here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch: it uses no axioms (Print Assumptions), and its transition table is this machine. It is their proof, on busycoq's definitions of a machine and of halting, and busycoq's maintainer has not yet reviewed it. Everything else on this page is what this repository found on its own, which by itself leaves the question open.

What this repository found on its own (background). Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps, the C simulator none in 109. The macro structure described below is observed in the simulation, not proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 24,776 cells have been visited and 14,654 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.189). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Nested counters
claims.text: Runs of 1 0^2 and of 1 0 1^2 0 grouped by markers 1 0 1^2 0^2; the first a-run grows by 6 while the first c-run shrinks by 2 between consecutive samples shown in the README (observed up to 10<sup>9</sup> steps).

claims.title: Slow growth
claims.text: Only the left side grows, 27,455 cells at 1.86·10<sup>9</sup> steps.

claims.title: Shift rules, for every n
claims.text: C crosses (100)^n to the right and leaves (110)^n; A crosses (001)^n and leaves (101)^n; E crosses (11010)^n and leaves (01010)^n.

claims.title: Size of the tape description (family screen)
claims.text: At the 8 records between 2.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.7·10<sup>10</sup> steps (first new leftmost or rightmost cell after each threshold 10<sup>6</sup>·4^k) the tape has 18,577 to 133,374 visited cells and compresses to 17 to 36 level-2 tokens (repeats of a word of at most 40 cells, then repeats of groups of such tokens).

claims.title: Proposed family: F06, block-list counters
claims.text: The description grows slowly: 19, 24, 36 and 35 level-2 tokens at the left-end records at 2.8·108, 109, 4.2·109 and 1.6·1010 steps. At the last one the tape is a block (010)^1537, then a list of blocks of the words 10101 and 100 (3 to 1,184 copies each) closed by markers 1010 (01)^3, and a last block (10101)^21602. A list of units of the same form whose number grows slowly is a list of counters (F06) and not a bounded description (F01): the token count nearly doubled on the screen.

claims.title: Halting, in this repository's own proofs
claims.text: Decided outside: busycoq pull request 106 proves in Rocq that it halts, after about 4.25·10<sup>47</sup> steps (compiled here, no axioms; see above). This repository proved no macro rule for it beyond the shift rules.

explainer.lede: It halts, after about 4.25·10<sup>47</sup> steps. The tape is made of two words in runs that behave like the digits of nested counters, several of them in base 3. Busycoq pull request 106 follows the run exactly, with proved shortcuts that jump over whole counter cycles, through 958,787,029,001 visits of the head to the left end, until it reads a 1 in state F.

facts.text: runs of two words behave like the levels of a counter
No halt in the C simulator; 24,776 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: An exact run, accelerated by proved counter shortcuts
html: The proof is busycoq pull request 106 by Alex Havrilla of DeepMind: a Rocq file of 115,070 lines (2.7 MB). About 22,000 lines are proof and the rest is a certificate, a long list of instructions. It was compiled here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch, in 383 seconds, and it uses no axioms (recorded in holdouts/external.json). Its main theorem is halt : halts tm c0: from the blank tape, the machine halts.

The shape. Write wn for the word w written n times. The proof watches the machine at hubs: the head at the left end of the tape in state E. At a hub the tape reads 001 0 1, then a list of items, then 0101. Most items are a pair of runs (001)a (01011)s, sometimes with the marker 01001 between them. These are the two words this page calls a and c, cut at a different place. There are also a few other items: a run of such pairs repeated, a run of a single short token, or a raw piece. All the counts are binary numbers, some near 1047.

The repeated step. The basic step goes from one hub to the next (step1Hub), and it is proved to match the machine for all counts. Doing it 958,787,029,001 times would be far too slow, so the proof adds shortcuts. Each is a function on the item list, proved for every value of its counts, that jumps over many hubs at once. A base-3 odometer counts through digit groups 011, 100 and 010. An eater consumes a run of transparent items. A slicer covers 12 hubs, removing 85 tokens per repeated pair. A wave covers 402 hubs: a front carry runs through the list in 6 regimes. Two mirror cycles cover 3,752 and 162 hubs. Fourteen operators in all (CertOp), with small bridges that run the raw machine for a short window.

The certificate. From the blank tape, 58 machine steps reach the first hub. The certificate then lists 90,940 operator applications in 20 parts. The computer checks each part with vm_compute: it applies the operators and compares with the item list written in the file. The lemma stepCert1_sound says every successful operator really is a run of the machine. In the last hub list the base-3 structure is plain to see: consecutive items have a-counts 126,800,055, 42,266,685, 14,088,895, 4,696,299, ..., each a third of the one before. From that hub a short raw run (runPipeRawHalt, 40 steps of fuel) ends with the head in state F reading a 1, the halting transition.

Computer and algebra. Proved by ordinary reasoning, for every value: the encoding of tapes as item lists, the one-hub step, and each of the 14 operators (odometer arithmetic, carry waves, mirror cycles). Checked by the computer: that the 90,940 steps of the certificate apply, with the exact numbers, and the final raw run. No part of the run is estimated or sampled. Every one of the about 4.25·1047 steps is covered by a proved rule.

sections.heading: Nested counters
html: Write a for 1 0^2 and c for 1 0 1^2 0. When the head is at the left end in state A, the tape reads, for example at step 513,296,770, A>0 0 1 0 1 0 a^465 1 0 c^86 1 0 1^2 0^2 a^21 1 0 a 1 0 c^8 1 0 1^2 0^2 a^7 1 0 a 1 0 c^63 1 0 1^2 0^2 a 1 0 a 1 0 c^1454 1^2 0 c^3018 1 0 1: runs of a and runs of c, grouped by the marker 1 0 1^2 0^2.

From one such sample to the next shown here (a few samples apart) the first run of a grows by 6 while the first run of c shrinks by 2, and the runs further right change more rarely, like the digits of a counter with several levels. The tape grows only to the left, and slowly (triage exponent 0.19): 27,455 cells at 1.86·109 steps.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine halts when it reads a 1 in state F (F1 is the halting transition). F is entered from D on a 1 (D1 = 1RF) and from E on a 0 (E0 = 1LF). It does halt: the proof of pull request 106 (first section) ends with F reading a 1, after about 4.25·1047 steps.

sections.heading: Shift rules over the runs
html: Runs of a and of c are crossed by shift rules proved for every length: C over (100)^n leaves (110)^n, A over (001)^n leaves (101)^n, and E over (11010)^n leaves (01010)^n. The counter map between left-end samples was not found here; the outside proof (first section) supplies it, as 14 proved operators on the item list.

sections.heading: Which family it belongs to
html: The 22 machines of family F09 (“bouncers over lists of counters, not yet classified”) were screened in one way. The machine runs from blank tape for 2·1010 steps; each time the tape reaches a new cell after a threshold, the tape is compressed twice: first repeats of one word, then repeats of groups of words. If the tape is a few growing blocks and a bounded rest, the number of level-2 tokens stays bounded while the tape grows. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.

The description grows slowly: 19, 24, 36 and 35 level-2 tokens at the left-end records at 2.8·108, 109, 4.2·109 and 1.6·1010 steps. At the last one the tape is a block (010)^1537, then a list of blocks of the words 10101 and 100 (3 to 1,184 copies each) closed by markers 1010 (01)^3, and a last block (10101)^21602.
A list of units of the same form whose number grows slowly is a list of counters (F06) and not a bounded description (F01): the token count nearly doubled on the screen.
Next step. The round rule on the list of pairs (a, b), sampled at the left-end records, and the rule that adds a unit.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.189). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 24,776 cells (260 left of the start, 24,423 right), with a density of 1s of 0.591.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: nested counters built from two words, growing left
summary: The tape is made of two words, 1 0^2 and 1 0 1^2 0, in runs separated by markers 1 0 1^2 0^2; the runs behave like nested counters, the outermost run on the left growing while inner ones are used up. Decided outside: busycoq PR 106 proves in Rocq that it halts (compiled here).
